root_cause.text: `drivers/pci/p2pdma.c:p2pmem_alloc_mmap()` kept a `VM_WARN_ON_ONCE_PAGE(!page_ref_count(page))` assertion that assumed newly allocated P2PDMA pages must have a nonzero refcount, but after commit `b7e282378773` their initial refcount was changed to zero, so the stale check falsely triggered a `CONFIG_DEBUG_VM` warning on a valid page state.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE text says `b7e282378773` “changed the initial page refcount of p2pdma page from one to zero,” yet `p2pmem_alloc_mmap()` still used `VM_WARN_ON_ONCE_PAGE(!page_ref_count(page))`, producing `page dumped because: VM_WARN_ON_ONCE_PAGE(!page_ref_count(page))` and a warning at `drivers/pci/p2pdma.c:240`; the patch fixes this by changing the predicate to `VM_WARN_ON_ONCE_PAGE(page_ref_count(page))`.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes `VM_WARN_ON_ONCE_PAGE(!page_ref_count(page), page);` to `VM_WARN_ON_ONCE_PAGE(page_ref_count(page), page);`, and the commit message explicitly says commit `b7e282378773` changed the initial P2PDMA page refcount from one to zero while `p2pmem_alloc_mmap()` still asserted the old condition, triggering `VM_WARN_ON_ONCE_PAGE(!page_ref_count(page))` warnings.

root_cause_review.feedback: The evidence and description show the bug is a wrong warning predicate after the refcount initialization changed, but the proposed root cause is internally inconsistent: it says the pages “start at 0, causing a false debug warning path” yet the original code warned on `!page_ref_count(page)`, which would trigger when refcount is 0; the actual issue was that the assertion was inverted relative to the intended state. The root cause should state that the check itself was stale/inverted and falsely warned on correctly zero-refcount P2PDMA pages, not that zero refcount “caused” the warning in a way that matches the old condition.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the page reference-count warning in p2pmem mmap allocation to detect unexpected nonzero refs on newly allocated pages.
intent_record.what: The condition passed to VM_WARN_ON_ONCE_PAGE was inverted: it changed from warning when page_ref_count(page) was zero to warning when page_ref_count(page) is nonzero, while leaving the rest of the mmap allocation logic unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the warning now triggers if the allocated page unexpectedly already has a reference count, instead of if it has none. This aligns the check with the stated assumption that newly allocated pages should not be in use by anyone else before set_page_count(page, 1) and vm_insert_page() are called.
